preconditions.expression: len(p) < len(t) and all(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' for c in t) and all(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' for c in p)
preconditions.description: Input words t and p consist of lowercase Latin letters, and |p| < |t|.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a_i <= len(t) for a_i in a) and len(a) == len(t) and len(set(a)) == len(t)
preconditions.description: The permutation a is a list of distinct indices from 1 to |t|, specifying the removal order.

preconditions.expression: any(all(t[i] == p[j] for i, j in zip(selected_indices, range(len(p)))) for selected_indices in combinations(range(len(t)), len(p)))
preconditions.description: It is guaranteed that p can be obtained by removing letters from t (i.e., p is a subsequence of t).

postconditions.expression: stdout == str(max_k) and (max_k == 0 or (max_k > 0 and all(t[a_i - 1] not in p or t[a_i - 1] in p and p.count(t[a_i - 1]) > p[:k].count(t[a_i - 1]) for k in range(1, max_k + 1) for a_i in a[:k]))) and (max_k == len(a) or not any(all(t[a_i - 1] == p[j] for a_i, j in zip(a[max_k:], range(len(p)))) for k in range(max_k + 1, len(a) + 1)))
postconditions.description: The output is the maximum number of letters Nastya can remove (max_k) such that after removing the first max_k letters in order a[0..max_k-1], the remaining letters in t can still form p as a subsequence. If max_k = len(a), then p is already formed after all removals.
